name: ask_user
description: Ask the person who gave you the task a question and wait for the answer. Use it only when you cannot proceed without it, or to get explicit consent (for example to open a pull request with failing checks). Be specific. `question` is always required, with or without `choices`: it is the sentence the person reads first. Whenever the answer is one of a few options, pass `choices` and never write the options as a list in your text: the person gets one form with a list of options per question and answers them together; their answers come back as the result. Give the form a short `title` and a `description` of why you ask (a sentence or two of plain text). Each entry of `choices` needs its own `question`; give every option a short `label` and a `description` that says what it means or what it costs, and mark the one you recommend with `recommended: true`. A question's `type` is `single` (radio buttons, the default; 2 to 12 options), `multiple` (checkboxes; 2 to 12; `min` and `max` say how many), `select` (a searchable list; 2 to 50 options), `images` (a deck of pictures; 2 to 16 options, each with `image` {sha256, alt}: the sha256 of an image file you shared in this conversation, never a URL) or `text` / `longText` (the person types the answer; no options). Five kinds fit what a list cannot: `confirm` (a yes or no, `yesLabel` and `noLabel` name the two buttons, `default` "yes" or "no" is the safe answer; use it for consent before something that cannot be undone), `number` (a decimal, `minValue`, `maxValue`, `step`, `unit`), `scale` (a rating of whole numbers from `from`, 0 or 1, to `to`, 2 to 10, with `fromLabel` and `toLabel` for the two ends), `date` (a day, YYYY-MM-DD, `minDate`, `maxDate`) and `rank` (the person puts 2 to 12 options in order, the best first). A number, a bound and a default are decimals, like 12.5; a screen that lacks a kind gets the nearest form. The answer to a form is checked against it: one that breaks a rule (a number out of range, a day outside its bounds, a rank that is not every option once) goes back to the person to fix, at most 5 times. Words the person typed instead of using the form reach you unchecked, and you read them. `help` is a line under the question, `default` is what is chosen at first, `allowOther` offers an "Other" the person can write, `freeInput` adds an "anything else" box. With a single possible answer, or none that you know, do not use `choices`: ask a plain question. There are at most 8 questions. An `id` or option `value` is 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits and `- _ . :`. Example: {"question": "A few things I need before I start.", "title": "Before I start", "description": "The migration depends on the database, so I need to know which one.", "choices": [{"id": "db", "question": "Which database?", "options": [{"label": "Postgres", "description": "Relational, the default", "recommended": true}, {"label": "MongoDB", "description": "Documents, no schema"}]}]} Without `choices` the question is plain text.

question.description: Required, even when `choices` is given: what you need to know, or the sentence that opens the form

title.description: The form's heading: a few words (with `choices`)

description.description: Why you are asking, in a sentence or two of plain text, no Markdown (with `choices`)

choices.description: Questions with fixed answers, asked together as one form (at most 8). Each needs `question` and, unless it is a typed answer, `options`. Omit for an open question.

id.description: A short id for the question (1 to 64 letters, digits, - _ . :), used in the answer; defaults to q1, q2, ...

help.description: A line under the question: what the options mean, or what the answer is for

type.description: How it is answered: single (radio buttons, the default), multiple (checkboxes), select (a searchable list), images (a deck of pictures), text (a short typed answer), longText (a longer one), confirm (yes or no), number (a decimal), scale (a rating between two ends), date (a day), rank (put the options in order)

options.description: The answers to pick from, each a label or {value, label, description, image, icon, recommended}: 2 to 12 for single, multiple and rank, 2 to 50 for select, 2 to 16 for images (each with an image); none for the other types

description.description: The option's subtitle: what it means or what it costs, in a short sentence

image.description: A picture of the option, for type "images": the sha256 of an image file you shared in this conversation, never a URL

alt.description: What the picture shows, in words

label.description: The option's title: a few words

recommended.description: Mark this option as the one you recommend

value.description: A short id for the option (1 to 64 letters, digits, - _ . :); made from the label when omitted

multiple.description: Several options may be picked (the same as type "multiple"; with select and images it lets several be picked)

allowOther.description: Offer an "Other" the person can write

required.description: The person must answer this one (the default)

default.description: What is chosen at first: an option's value or label, or a list of them for several; the words a typed question starts with; for confirm "yes" or "no" (the safe answer), for number a decimal, for scale a point, for date a day, for rank every option's value once, in the order the list starts in

min.description: The fewest options to pick, when several may be picked

max.description: The most options to pick, when several may be picked

from.description: scale only: the first point, 0 or 1 (1 when absent)

fromLabel.description: scale only: the words at the first point (Not at all)

maxDate.description: date only: the last day allowed, YYYY-MM-DD

maxValue.description: number only: the most, a decimal

minDate.description: date only: the first day allowed, YYYY-MM-DD

minValue.description: number only: the least, a decimal like 0 or "2.5"

noLabel.description: confirm only: the words of the no button ("No" when absent)

step.description: number only: the answer is the least (or 0) plus a whole number of these, above zero

to.description: scale only, required: the last point, 2 to 10, above `from`

toLabel.description: scale only: the words at the last point (Certainly)

unit.description: number only: what the number counts, shown beside the box (EUR, kg)

yesLabel.description: confirm only: the words of the yes button ("Yes" when absent)

freeInput.description: Add an "anything else" box to the form; its words come back as the note of the answer

submitLabel.description: The words of the button (at most 40 characters)
